people rules › knowledge
a person knows a fact only if they witnessed it (§05: a clear sightline within 13 m) or were told it along a tie. At the start nobody knows anything about the cell (person.memoryAtStart). The one thing a person starts knowing about others is listed in needsKnown. The cell is known by face only: a witness remembers the Fixer's face (§03), never a name.
identity in play: face; learned by: witnessed, told; the cell at the start: nothing
needs known at the start: a keeper knows the needs of workmate and unit-regular (§08 economy: café owner tips needs before Scout listens)
From DF's rumour rule (a fact exists only for those who saw it or were told) and Adams 2017 (identity stored per observer as alias, name or face). Only face is in play: the Talker's facts are a face, a car and a place-time, and §05 investigators hop by place and time, not by name. needsKnown makes §08's tip rule checkable from the cast: a keeper knows the need of each workmate and of each person with a regular tie into their unit, so a turned keeper saves the Listen (42 s) on each. How a fact spreads at runtime (told, along which ties, how fast) is Keel's rule, not this file's.

people rules › mix
the culture baseline is the cast row: an area × occupation's temperament weights. No temperament may hold more than rowMaxShare of a row's weight, and a unit with whenStaffAtLeast staff or more carries at least unitMinDistinct temperaments.
row cap 60% of a row's weight; a unit of 3+ staff carries at least 2 temperaments
§09 risk: sameness (Watch Dogs: Legion); §04 Hero and Menace turn different halves of the city
DF draws each person from a culture baseline, then lets them deviate. Our baseline is the cast row, and this cap keeps every person from being the baseline. At any workplace of three or more there are two kinds of person, so there are two ways in at two prices, which serves the pillar orchestrate the city. 0.6 and 3 are [S].
